Yang Jing (; d. 1382), a native of Hefei, Anhui, was a Ming dynasty general.
During his early years, Yang Jing pledged his allegiance to Zhu Yuanzhang and joined the army in Jiqing (present-day Nanjing). After conquering Changzhou, he was appointed as the Vice Commander of the Guards (). He then went to Wuzhou and other places and was eventually promoted to the position of Assistant Administrator of the Huguang Province (), stationed in Jiangling. Later, he led an attack on Hunan and was promoted to the Province's Manager of Governmental Affairs (). In 1367, along with other generals, including Zhou Dexing () and Zhang Bin (), Yang Jing attacked Guangxi. The following year, he captured Yongzhou and Jingjiang, pacifying Guangxi. He then joined Tang He and Xu Da in an attack on Shanxi. For his achievements, he was granted the title of Marquis of Yingyang (). In 1370, he led a delegation to Sichuan to persuade the Xia state to surrender, but this mission failed. Yang Jing died in 1382 and was posthumously honored as Duke of Rui (), with the posthumous name of Wuxin ().
Yang Jing had two sons, Yang Tong Yang Tong () and Yang Da (). Yang Tong succeeded to his father's title. In 1387, he led surrendered Mongol troops to garrison Yunnan; however, many deserted en route. As a result, he was demoted to Commander of Puding Garrison. Yang Jing's second son, Yang Da, held a minor post.
